# Gelabber v0.7.1

Integrated through the PRs #280-#285, #292, #300-#303, #305-#317 and #319 into
`v0.7.1` and the version PR into `main`.

**Operators: read "Upgrade notes" first.** Four database migrations run on
the first start (no rollback without a backup). Account mail stays off until
you configure an SMTP relay. Take the new `compose.yaml`, `Caddyfile` and
`.env.example` from this checkout and recreate the proxy.

## Accounts

- Address confirmation and password reset by mail (#284). Off until the
  operator sets `SMTP_HOST`; until then registration works as before.
  - With mail on, registration sends a confirmation link (valid 24 h) and
    signs nobody in. Confirming asks for the account's password as well.
  - "Passwort vergessen?" on the sign-in page sends a reset link (valid 1 h,
    single use). A reset ends every session of the account.
  - Registration answers the same whether or not an address is known, and
    at most 5 mails per address and hour go out.

## Notifications

- New switch **"Inhalt in Benachrichtigungen verbergen"** in the
  notification settings (#280). Web Push and the page's own notifications
  then only say "Neue Nachricht von …", without text or conversation. It
  applies to every device of the account; notifications already on screen
  are closed when it is turned on.
- Mention follow-ups (#283): `@here` inside a link no longer pings, an edit
  that keeps `@here` reaches the same people as before, the unread mention
  count is faster, and a brand-new conversation follows its own and its
  server's notification setting right away.
- Read sync and Web Push follow-ups (#282): "mark everything as read" no
  longer fails when a channel is deleted at the same moment, mention pushes
  only go to people still in the server, and subscriptions a push service
  refuses are cleaned up without dropping everything on a server-side fault.

## Calls

- **Push-to-talk** (#285): voice settings offer "Sprachaktivierung" or
  "Push-to-Talk" with any key or side mouse button and a release delay. In
  the browser the key works while the tab has the focus. The desktop app
  hears it globally during a call: on Windows through a keyboard/mouse hook,
  on Linux through the GlobalShortcuts portal (KDE and GNOME ask once; on
  Hyprland bind `gelabber-desktop:push-to-talk` in `hyprland.conf`).
- Desktop app: playback above 100 % is limited after the mix instead of
  clipping each loud speaker (#281).
- Desktop app: if switching to another microphone or speaker during a call
  fails, the microphone no longer goes silent. The app goes back to the
  previous device, or to the system default if that one was unplugged (#311).
- Desktop app: the pop-out video window shows rotated streams (for example a
  phone held upright) the right way up (#311).

## Video codecs

- The media server tells every client which video codecs all receivers in
  the room can decode, and a publisher picks the best of them: H.264 where
  the device encodes it in hardware, otherwise VP8 (#292). Rooms with a
  receiver that cannot decode H.264 stay on VP8.
- Desktop app, Linux: H.264 decoding on the GPU through the system's
  GStreamer (NVIDIA, VA-API), with a software fallback (#300).
- Desktop app, Windows: H.264 through Media Foundation (NVENC, AMF,
  Quick Sync, else Microsoft's encoder; DXVA decoding) (#301). Windows N
  without the Media Feature Pack stays on VP8.
- The desktop packages no longer ship an H.264 codec of their own (#302):
  H.264 comes only from the system (GStreamer on Linux, Media Foundation on
  Windows). Without a system codec, calls use VP8. The third-party notices no
  longer list FFmpeg and OpenH264.

## Security

- **Rate limits behind a proxy** (#315): the bundled Caddy now believes
  `X-Forwarded-For` from the peers in `GELABBER_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (default
  `private_ranges`). With a proxy in front ("Small diff", Nginx, …), all users
  no longer share one sign-in window. The API counts IPv6 clients per /64,
  its limiter memory is bounded, session keys are hashed, and malformed
  session cookies count against the client address. See the upgrade notes
  for the proxy settings.
- The web image sends a Content-Security-Policy for scripts (a hash for the
  theme bootstrap, `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` for noise suppression, frames only
  from youtube-nocookie, no framing of the app), plus
  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`,
  `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and a Permissions-Policy (#308).
- The media SFU closes control WebSockets that have not joined a voice
  channel within 10 s of opening or of leaving one (`MEDIA_JOIN_DEADLINE_MS`
  changes the limit), and no longer serves the public `/media/metrics` alias
  (#307).
- Avatar and banner uploads count against `API_UPLOAD_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_DAY`,
  and the host of `turn://host` entries in `TURN_URLS` goes on the
  link-preview deny list (#306).
- Desktop app: after switching servers, the previous server's pages can no
  longer use the app's media, tray, push-to-talk or update commands (#311).
- Backups: with `GELABBER_BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT` set, `deploy/backup.sh`
  encrypts the dump and the MinIO archive while writing them, so no plain
  text touches the disk. `SHA256SUMS` lists the `*.age` files, and a
  malformed recipient aborts before anything is stopped (#313).
- The bundled coturn entry script no longer falls back to the old public TURN
  password; Compose already required `TURN_PASSWORD` (#313).

## Fixes and performance

- Plain-HTTP test mode (`API_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP`): the web client and the
  desktop app no longer fail every request because insecure origins have no
  Web Locks. In this mode browser tabs do not coordinate sign-in and sign-out,
  and voice and video in the browser still need TLS (#312). This reverses the
  v0.6.0 note that called the failure deliberate.
- After a reconnect resync or a new DM, the web client no longer reloads the
  history of every DM already listed (#312).
- The gateway uses far fewer database connections per open WebSocket, and the
  API's Postgres pool defaults to 20 connections, set with
  `API_DB_MAX_CONNECTIONS` (#316).
- A message deleted twice at the same time produces only one delete event
  (#306).
- Deleting a server or channel no longer searches notification settings
  across every user, and a presence snapshot reads all statuses in one Redis
  round trip (#317).
- Media: a worker that never confirms a native close restarts the service
  after 10 s instead of being polled forever, join tickets reuse the engine's
  Redis connection, and clients get `gone` or `unauthorized` before the
  socket closes (#310).
- Internal: one source for the Redis authority and Go Live key formats, and
  the legacy `gb:deny` key is gone (#305); no import cycles in the web client,
  guarded by a test (#309).

## Build

- CI: pull requests no longer evict the shared Rust and Docker caches, and
  the Linux desktop job stops building the mediasoup worker twice (#303).
- All GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs and kept current by
  Dependabot (#313).

## Upgrade notes

- **Back up first** (`deploy/backup.sh`) or pause Watchtower: migrations
  0020 (notification privacy), 0021 (account mail: `email_verified_at`,
  `registration_pending`, `account_tokens`; existing accounts count as
  confirmed), 0023 (`messages.here_users` and a partial index on messages;
  message writes wait while the index builds) and 0024 (an index on
  `notification_settings`) run on start.
- **Update the checkout and recreate the proxy.** Watchtower swaps only the
  images, so bring the server checkout to the release for the new
  `compose.yaml`, `Caddyfile` and `.env.example` (`git pull`, or
  `git fetch --tags && git checkout v0.7.1`), then run `docker compose up -d`
  and `docker compose up -d --no-deps --force-recreate proxy`. The bundled
  Caddy then trusts `X-Forwarded-For` from `GELABBER_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (default
  `private_ranges`).
  - Behind a CDN or tunnel, add its ranges.
  - Under the default `private_ranges`, LAN clients can choose the address
    they are counted under when they reach the bundled Caddy directly, or
    through a proxy that appends to `X-Forwarded-For`. With rootless Docker
    (default port driver), Docker Desktop, or IPv6 to an IPv4-only Compose
    network, *any* client that reaches the port can do this, also through a
    proxy container in front. See "Client addresses" in `deploy/README.md`
    for the remedies before recreating the proxy. Behind a proxy that
    overwrites the header, all LAN clients share that proxy's window. The per-account lockout and the per-address mail limit
    still apply. Setting the exact proxy or gateway address avoids both
    cases. `GELABBER_TRUSTED_PROXIES=` trusts no proxy.
  - Homelab: add `header_up X-Forwarded-For {client_ip}` to the API
    upstreams of your own Caddy.
- **Metrics:** if you scraped `/media/metrics` through your own proxy, scrape
  the media service directly (`media:8081/metrics`, as the bundled Prometheus
  does).
- **Own CSP:** if your proxy adds a CSP with `connect-src` or `default-src`,
  it must still allow `ipc:` and `http://ipc.localhost` for the desktop app
  (see `deploy/README.md`).
- **Upload quota:** a user who has used up the day's upload quota cannot
  change avatar or banner until the next UTC day.
- **Backups:** backups made by 0.7.0 or earlier list the plain file names in
  `SHA256SUMS`, so check those after decrypting. A backup directory without
  `SHA256SUMS`, or with `*.part` files, is incomplete. With
  `GELABBER_BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT` set, `backup.sh` now aborts before stopping
  anything if `age` is missing or the recipient is invalid; check cron-driven
  backups after setting it.
- **DB pool:** if you raise `API_DB_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, keep it well below
  Postgres' `max_connections` (100 in the bundled Postgres) and recreate the
  API afterwards.
- **Account mail** stays off until you set, in `.env`:

  ```bash
  SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.org
  SMTP_SECURITY=starttls        # starttls (587, default), tls (465) or none (25)
  SMTP_PORT=                    # only if not the default for SMTP_SECURITY
  SMTP_USERNAME=…               # both or neither
  SMTP_PASSWORD=…
  MAIL_FROM="Gelabber <noreply@example.org>"
  APP_PUBLIC_URL=https://chat.example.org
  ```

  The new `compose.yaml` passes these through. The API refuses to start with
  a password over `none`, without `MAIL_FROM` or `APP_PUBLIC_URL`, or with an
  `http://` public URL while `API_COOKIE_SECURE=true`. Mail links point at
  `APP_PUBLIC_URL`. See `deploy/README.md`.
- **Desktop, Linux (Arch):** new optional dependencies for H.264 from the
  system: `gst-plugins-bad` (h264parse, NVIDIA), `gst-plugin-va` (Intel/AMD)
  and `gst-libav` (software decoding). Without them calls use VP8.
- **Desktop, Windows:** the installer and `latest.json` are attached to this
  release; 0.7.0 apps offer the update.

  AMD, Intel) and the CPU load in a real call; mail delivery through a real
  relay.
- Open issues: #165 (desktop tracker), #195 (rest: session lifetime), #290
